articles.title: Argentina: la política y la pobreza en medio de la visita de León XIV
articles.summary: Contener los discursos de León XIV referidos a la deuda social podría resultar incómodo para el gobierno de Milei. Mientras tanto, el pueblo argentino aguarda expectante la llegada de un pontífice después de cuatro décadas.
articles.body_text: Cuando León XIV aterrice este domingo 8 en el Aeroparque Jorge Newbery de Buenos Aires, se encontrará con una Argentina distinta a la que vio Juan Pablo II, el último Papa en visitar este país cuarenta años atrás. En la década de los 80, nueve de cada diez argentinos profesaba la religión católica. Hoy, las mediciones más recientes se ubican en torno al 60%. La caída se explica, en parte, por el crecimiento de los movimientos evangélicos y los que no tienen afiliación religiosa. También se topará con una cara de la pobreza más visible. Mientras que, en 1987, los pobres no superaban el 16%, el reporte emitido este viernes por el INDEC (Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censos), refiere que el 34,4% de la población no llega a cubrir sus necesidades básicas. La situación económica asoma como la principal preocupación en la ciudadanía. En una última encuesta de la UBA (Universidad de Buenos Aires), sobre las expectativas de la visita papal, casi la mitad de los entrevistados espera que el pontífice priorice la agenda social por encima de temas como la paz internacional o transparencia de la iglesia. “Creo que conforme el Papa haga referencia a la pobreza, a la crisis, puede terminar siendo una visita incómoda para el Gobierno”, refiere Mariano De Vedía, periodista de La Nación especializado en la cobertura eclesiástica. Además de las actividades protocolares, el itinerario de León XIV incluye compromisos que podrían generar tensiones con la gestión de Javier Milei. El Sumo Pontífice se reunirá con líderes sindicales y representantes de movimiento sociales, con quienes el Ejecutivo ha tenido fricciones. Asimismo, visitará el Cottolengo de Don Orione, un albergue dedicado al cuidado de personas con discapacidad. El desfinanciamiento de programas y el recorte de pensiones, convirtió al sector de la discapacidad en uno de los grupos más expuestos a la política de ajuste fiscal. “Este gesto del Papa se puede prestar a múltiples lecturas. En el contexto actual, esta visita al Cottolengo tiene mucha trascendencia simbólica”, anota De Vedía. El cronista eclesiástico refiere que, pese a que el Papa asuma una postura neutral, su presencia podría quedar atravesada por las disputas de la política argentina. En esa línea indica estar atentos al juego del peronista Axel Kicillof, Gobernador de la Provincia de Buenos Aires y uno de los principales competidores de Milei en la carrera electoral de 2027. Según De Vedía, el ex ministro de Cristina Fernández podría intentar sacar provecho de esta visita, al darse dentro de su jurisdicción. “Durante la preparación de la recepción, tanto oficialismo como oposición han priorizado la sana convivencia, pero eso no quiere decir que el clima no se desborde cuando el Papa esté entre nosotros”, indica De Vedía. Una relación compleja En el ejercicio del poder, Milei ha mantenido una relación tensa y distante con la Iglesia local. El arzobispo de Buenos Aires, Jorge García Cuerva, en diversos momentos, cuestionó los ataques a la prensa, reclamó por jubilaciones dignas y criticó el lenguaje agresivo que emplean figuras del oficialismo en las redes sociales. Por su parte, el mandatario, desde marzo de 2024, no atiende las solicitudes de audiencia con la cúpula eclesiástica. Este congelamiento dista del trato fluido que tiene el líder libertario con el mundo evangélico. En los últimos dos años, inauguró templos en provincias y recibió a delegaciones de pastores en Casa Rosada. “Algunos ven esta proximidad como una provocación al mundo católico, pero también puede ser cierto olfato de Milei en ver si puede capitalizar algo del alcance que los evangélicos tienen en las clases populares”, indica Diego Mauro, historiador e investigador Conicet (Consejo Nacional de Investigaciones Científicas y Técnicas). Para los especialistas, pese al distanciamiento con los líderes católicos locales, el Gobierno buscará evitar fricciones durante la estadía de León XIV y priorizará el tono protocolar. “La estrategia que se está viendo es no confrontar, sino tratar de presentar la visita como exitosa desde el punto de vista logístico y de impacto internacional”, anota Mauro. El historiador, especializado en religión, refiere que la reducción de la masa católica no afectará la capacidad de convocatoria que tiene el Papa como líder espiritual. En las últimas semanas se agotaron las plazas hoteleras de Córdoba y Luján, lugares donde se ofrecerán misas multitudinarias. El Gobierno estima que aproximadamente 7 millones de personas se movilizarán durante los cuatro días de la visita apostólica. Por ello, la ministra de Seguridad, Alejandra Monteoliva, detalló que alistan el “operativo logístico más grande de la historia”. La llegada de León XIV también tiene un tono reivindicador para los fieles argentinos. Ante la frustración de no recibir a al Papa Francisco durante los 12 años de su pontificado, esta gira puede entenderse como la posibilidad de saldar una deuda. “Creo que el mismo León XIV piensa esta visita como un tributo a Francisco”, dice Mauro. Por la proximidad que tuvo con el pontífice argentino, en los discursos e intervenciones se esperan referencias explícitas a la figura de Francisco. “León se alineó al proyecto de sinodalidad, de una Iglesia con opción preferencial por los pobres. Es la misma vertiente teológica”, agrega el especialista. Por esa línea pastoral, se espera que el Sumo Pontífice dedique buena parte de sus intervenciones a las deudas con los sectores vulnerables. En cada uno de los actos masivos, la Iglesia ha destinado espacios preferenciales para que personas de bajos recursos participen de las homilías. El desafío del Gobierno será tratar de minimizar las tensiones y el costo político de lo que el Papa pueda decir. “A fin de cuentas, el Papa se irá y la política argentina retomará su senda habitual de confrontación”, cierra De Vedía.

articles.title: ¿Noviembre tiene feriados? Revisa los días libres de labores este 2026 en el Perú
articles.summary: Tras el feriado del primero de noviembre, te invitamos a conocer si hay otros feriados o días no laborables en el mes de noviembre. Conócelo todos en la siguiente nota.
articles.body_text: Los días libres son una oportunidad para compartir tiempo en familia, organizar actividades personales o realizar pequeños viajes sin las obligaciones habituales del trabajo. En noviembre de 2026, el calendario peruano contempla fechas de descanso que deben distinguirse entre feriados nacionales y días no laborables establecidos de manera extraordinaria. Estas últimas disposiciones están vinculadas con la visita del papa León XIV al Perú y comprenden jornadas y horarios específicos en Lima, Callao y otras regiones del país. Además, no todos los trabajadores tendrán las mismas condiciones para acceder a estos descansos, pues algunas medidas requieren compensar posteriormente las horas que se dejen de trabajar. Conoce qué fechas están previstas para noviembre, en qué lugares se aplicarán y cuáles son las diferencias que debes tener en cuenta antes de organizar tus actividades. El calendario de noviembre tiene un feriado nacional, el pasado 1 de noviembre, día de todos los santos, sin embargo; también cuenta con días NO laborables según lo indica la ley. Estas últimas fueron oficializadas mediante el Decreto Supremo N.º 020-2026-TR, publicado en el diario oficial El Peruano. El calendario contempla las siguientes fechas: La compensación dependerá del sector laboral. En las entidades públicas, las horas pendientes deberán recuperarse dentro de los diez días posteriores al descanso o cuando lo determine el titular de cada institución, de acuerdo con las necesidades del servicio. En las empresas privadas, empleadores y trabajadores podrán acordar cómo reponer el tiempo no trabajado. Si no consiguen llegar a un consenso, el empleador establecerá las condiciones para realizar la compensación correspondiente. Aunque ambas fechas permiten interrumpir las actividades habituales, tienen condiciones distintas. El feriado constituye un descanso obligatorio reconocido por ley y no requiere recuperar las horas que correspondían a esa jornada. En cambio, los días no laborables suelen estar dirigidos principalmente al sector público y contemplan la recuperación posterior del tiempo pendiente. Para los trabajadores privados, su aplicación depende del acuerdo entre empleadores y trabajadores. Según la Cámara de Comercio de Lima (CCL), si un empleado trabaja en un día feriado debido a necesidades de la empresa o rotación de turnos, y no recibe un día libre en sustitución, debe recibir una compensación económica equivalente a tres veces su salario habitual por esa jornada laboral. Esto se debe a tres conceptos: No cumplir con el pago adicional o negar la compensación de descanso constituye una infracción muy grave en materia laboral. Las sanciones económicas varían según el tipo de empresa, y pueden ir desde poco más de 1.000 soles hasta superar los 24.000.

articles.title: Fiscalía de Paraguay imputa y pide prisión para expresidente Peña por crisis bancaria
articles.summary: La Fiscalía de Paraguay solicitó este sábado que se ordene la prisión preventiva contra el expresidente Santiago Peña, al que imputó formalmente por presunta lesión de confianza y administración en provecho propio durante su comparecencia dentro de la investigación por el cierre de Ueno bank, una entidad a la que ha sido vinculado el exmandatario y cuyo caso provocó su destitución.
articles.body_text: La Fiscalía de Paraguay solicitó este sábado que se ordene la prisión preventiva contra el expresidente Santiago Peña, al que imputó formalmente por presunta lesión de confianza y administración en provecho propio durante su comparecencia dentro de la investigación por el cierre de Ueno bank, una entidad a la que ha sido vinculado el exmandatario y cuyo caso provocó su destitución. Peña fue detenido el viernes poco después de haber sido hallado culpable en un juicio político por “mal desempeño de funciones” tras la disolución por problemas de insolvencia de Ueno, un banco con 2,94 millones de clientes, entre ellos importantes instituciones estatales cuyos fondos quedaron congelados. Tras la solicitud del Ministerio Público, un juez deberá determinar, en una audiencia de imposición de medidas, si acepta el pedido de los fiscales. Según el acta de imputación, el exmandatario está acusado por presunta lesión de confianza como instigador y por administración en provecho propio en calidad de autor. El documento indica que el expresidente “habría intervenido en circunstancias relacionadas con la colocación, renovación y permanencia de importantes sumas de dinero provenientes de entidades públicas y previsionales” en Ueno bank, una entidad con cuyo grupo empresarial Peña “habría mantenido una relación económica y corporativa previa”. Peña era accionista de Ueno Holding, un conglomerado del Grupo Vásquez que poseía, entre otras empresas, a Ueno bank. En marzo de 2025 vendió esa participación, detalló la acusación de los diputados que promovieron el juicio político en su contra. Ueno bank, añade el documento de la Fiscalía, habría recibido esos recursos públicos “mientras desarrollaba operaciones crediticias con sociedades presuntamente vinculadas a su grupo económico”, en las que “fueron identificadas observaciones e irregularidades por parte de los órganos de supervisión del Banco Central”. El Ministerio Público también imputó y pidió la prisión preventiva contra el expresidente del Banco Central de Paraguay (BCP) Carlos Carvallo, por presunta lesión de confianza, producción inmediata de documentos públicos de contenido falso y administración en provecho propio, en calidad de autor. Carvallo se presentó en la noche del viernes ante las autoridades y fue arrestado. El exfuncionario presidió la Financiera Ueno, de la que nació Ueno bank, antes de asumir en 2023 la jefatura de la entidad emisora, cuyo directorio autorizó “83 días después” de su designación la creación de la finiquitada entidad bancaria, explicaron los diputados en su acusación. Durante la administración de Peña, el Instituto de Previsión Social (IPS), una de las principales cajas pensionales del país, invirtió unos 355 millones de dólares en Ueno, que también administraba las cuentas de unos 32.000 jubilados. Por este caso, la Fiscalía también ha imputado a 27 personas, entre ellas Miguel Vásquez, uno de los fundadores de Ueno bank, quien este viernes fue trasladado junto a otros cinco directivos a cárceles para procesados.

articles.title: Tumbes: Oficina Regional de Gestión del Riesgo reporta vías afectadas y más de 10 quebradas activadas por intensas lluvias
articles.summary: El COEN reporta 13 almacenes para atender a los damnificados, mientras el Ejército realiza labores de limpieza y descolmatación en la región.
articles.body_text: Las intensas lluvias registradas en Tumbes continúan causando estragos en la región. Así lo informó a El Comercio el ingeniero Juan Carlos Ramírez Astudillo, jefe de la Oficina Regional de Gestión del Riesgo de Desastres (Ofregerd) del Gobierno Regional de Tumbes e integrante del Centro de Operaciones de Emergencia Nacional (COEN). El especialista indicó que las vías del distrito de San Juan de la Virgen permanecen afectadas como consecuencia de las lluvias e inundaciones. Asimismo, señaló que varias quebradas se encuentran activadas en la región, entre ellas Santa Rosa, Peña Blanca, Cardalitos, Belén, Cabuyal, La Capitana, Siete de Junio, Señor de los Milagros, Quebrada Seca, Fernández, Faical, El Tutumo, Mariátegui, Coloma, Las Peñas, Cafeterías y Miraflores. “Actualmente contamos con 13 almacenes al servicio de la población afectada, además de palas, retroexcavadoras, camiones cisterna y volquetes. De la mano de profesionales, tratamos de ayudar y monitorear este periodo lluvioso”, indicó. Ramírez Astudillo señaló que, tras la supervisión de la presidenta de la República, Keiko Fujimori, en la región, se dispuso que el Ejército del Perú también participe en las labores para enfrentar los efectos del fenómeno de El Niño. “Recomendamos a la población evitar transitar por las quebradas activas, porque hacerlo puede ocasionar la pérdida de vidas. Trataremos de hacer lo mejor posible ante cualquier embate de la naturaleza”, concluyó. Acciones El COEN informó que el Ejército del Perú implementó y acondicionó la infraestructura sanitaria del colegio María Mafalda Lama Lama, ubicado en el barrio El Pacífico, cuyas instalaciones funcionan como sede de un hospital de campaña temporal para atender emergencias. Asimismo, personal de la Brigada de Intervención Rápida para Desastres del Batallón de Tanques N.° 223, de la 9.ª Brigada Blindada, reanudó las labores de apoyo en el distrito de Canoas de Punta Sal, donde realiza trabajos de limpieza de vías y descolmatación de canales, en coordinación con las autoridades locales. Por otro lado, la Brigada de Intervención Rápida para Desastres del Batallón de Infantería Motorizado N.° 23, de la 1.ª Brigada de Infantería, trasladó ayuda humanitaria al albergue temporal instalado en el polideportivo Alberto Terranova, en el barrio San José. En tanto, la Compañía de Intervención Rápida para Desastres del Batallón de Tanques N.° 222, de la 9.ª Brigada Blindada, reanudó las labores de apoyo en el distrito de Zorritos, donde realiza trabajos de limpieza de canales. Asimismo, la losa deportiva de la institución educativa El Gran Chilimasa, ubicada en el distrito de Aguas Verdes, provincia de Zarumilla, fue acondicionada como albergue temporal. Por su parte, la organización internacional World Vision Perú, en coordinación con la UGEL de Zarumilla, entregó kits para la remoción de escombros y limpieza a las instituciones educativas N.° 069, N.° 127 Julio Salvador Izquierdo Puell y N.° 112, con el objetivo de recuperar sus espacios educativos y prepararlos ante posibles situaciones de emergencia. Atención médica Con el objetivo de garantizar la continuidad de la atención médica en Tumbes, el Seguro Social de Salud (EsSalud) suscribió un acuerdo para utilizar temporalmente áreas no inundables del Proyecto Especial Binacional Puyango-Tumbes. Estos espacios permitirán atender a pacientes y ampliar la capacidad de los servicios de salud durante el periodo más crítico de lluvias. Tras una visita técnica conjunta, ambas instituciones verificaron que el complejo reúne las condiciones necesarias para brindar atención y se encuentra fuera del alcance de las aguas pluviales. Como parte de esta estrategia de respuesta sanitaria, EsSalud también estableció una alianza con el Ejército del Perú para planificar el traslado oportuno de pacientes, insumos médicos y medicamentos esenciales. Esta medida busca garantizar la asistencia a la población en caso de que las inundaciones, los huaicos o la activación de quebradas interrumpan la conectividad vial en la región.

articles.title: ¿Noviembre tiene feriados? Revisa los días libres de labores este 2026 en el Perú
articles.summary: Tras el feriado del primero de noviembre, te invitamos a conocer si hay otros feriados o días no laborables en el mes de noviembre. Conócelo todos en la siguiente nota.
articles.body_text: Los días libres son una oportunidad para compartir tiempo en familia, organizar actividades personales o realizar pequeños viajes sin las obligaciones habituales del trabajo. En noviembre de 2026, el calendario peruano contempla fechas de descanso que deben distinguirse entre feriados nacionales y días no laborables establecidos de manera extraordinaria. Estas últimas disposiciones están vinculadas con la visita del papa León XIV al Perú y comprenden jornadas y horarios específicos en Lima, Callao y otras regiones del país. Además, no todos los trabajadores tendrán las mismas condiciones para acceder a estos descansos, pues algunas medidas requieren compensar posteriormente las horas que se dejen de trabajar. Conoce qué fechas están previstas para noviembre, en qué lugares se aplicarán y cuáles son las diferencias que debes tener en cuenta antes de organizar tus actividades. El calendario de noviembre tiene un feriado nacional, el pasado 1 de noviembre, día de todos los santos, sin embargo; también cuenta con días NO laborables según lo indica la ley. Estas últimas fueron oficializadas mediante el Decreto Supremo N.º 020-2026-TR, publicado en el diario oficial El Peruano. El calendario contempla las siguientes fechas: La compensación dependerá del sector laboral. En las entidades públicas, las horas pendientes deberán recuperarse dentro de los diez días posteriores al descanso o cuando lo determine el titular de cada institución, de acuerdo con las necesidades del servicio. En las empresas privadas, empleadores y trabajadores podrán acordar cómo reponer el tiempo no trabajado. Si no consiguen llegar a un consenso, el empleador establecerá las condiciones para realizar la compensación correspondiente. Aunque ambas fechas permiten interrumpir las actividades habituales, tienen condiciones distintas. El feriado constituye un descanso obligatorio reconocido por ley y no requiere recuperar las horas que correspondían a esa jornada. En cambio, los días no laborables suelen estar dirigidos principalmente al sector público y contemplan la recuperación posterior del tiempo pendiente. Para los trabajadores privados, su aplicación depende del acuerdo entre empleadores y trabajadores. Según la Cámara de Comercio de Lima (CCL), si un empleado trabaja en un día feriado debido a necesidades de la empresa o rotación de turnos, y no recibe un día libre en sustitución, debe recibir una compensación económica equivalente a tres veces su salario habitual por esa jornada laboral. Esto se debe a tres conceptos: No cumplir con el pago adicional o negar la compensación de descanso constituye una infracción muy grave en materia laboral. Las sanciones económicas varían según el tipo de empresa, y pueden ir desde poco más de 1.000 soles hasta superar los 24.000.

articles.title: Fiscalía de Paraguay imputa y pide prisión para expresidente Peña por crisis bancaria
articles.summary: La Fiscalía de Paraguay solicitó este sábado que se ordene la prisión preventiva contra el expresidente Santiago Peña, al que imputó formalmente por presunta lesión de confianza y administración en provecho propio durante su comparecencia dentro de la investigación por el cierre de Ueno bank, una entidad a la que ha sido vinculado el exmandatario y cuyo caso provocó su destitución.
articles.body_text: La Fiscalía de Paraguay solicitó este sábado que se ordene la prisión preventiva contra el expresidente Santiago Peña, al que imputó formalmente por presunta lesión de confianza y administración en provecho propio durante su comparecencia dentro de la investigación por el cierre de Ueno bank, una entidad a la que ha sido vinculado el exmandatario y cuyo caso provocó su destitución. Peña fue detenido el viernes poco después de haber sido hallado culpable en un juicio político por “mal desempeño de funciones” tras la disolución por problemas de insolvencia de Ueno, un banco con 2,94 millones de clientes, entre ellos importantes instituciones estatales cuyos fondos quedaron congelados. Tras la solicitud del Ministerio Público, un juez deberá determinar, en una audiencia de imposición de medidas, si acepta el pedido de los fiscales. Según el acta de imputación, el exmandatario está acusado por presunta lesión de confianza como instigador y por administración en provecho propio en calidad de autor. El documento indica que el expresidente “habría intervenido en circunstancias relacionadas con la colocación, renovación y permanencia de importantes sumas de dinero provenientes de entidades públicas y previsionales” en Ueno bank, una entidad con cuyo grupo empresarial Peña “habría mantenido una relación económica y corporativa previa”. Peña era accionista de Ueno Holding, un conglomerado del Grupo Vásquez que poseía, entre otras empresas, a Ueno bank. En marzo de 2025 vendió esa participación, detalló la acusación de los diputados que promovieron el juicio político en su contra. Ueno bank, añade el documento de la Fiscalía, habría recibido esos recursos públicos “mientras desarrollaba operaciones crediticias con sociedades presuntamente vinculadas a su grupo económico”, en las que “fueron identificadas observaciones e irregularidades por parte de los órganos de supervisión del Banco Central”. El Ministerio Público también imputó y pidió la prisión preventiva contra el expresidente del Banco Central de Paraguay (BCP) Carlos Carvallo, por presunta lesión de confianza, producción inmediata de documentos públicos de contenido falso y administración en provecho propio, en calidad de autor. Carvallo se presentó en la noche del viernes ante las autoridades y fue arrestado. El exfuncionario presidió la Financiera Ueno, de la que nació Ueno bank, antes de asumir en 2023 la jefatura de la entidad emisora, cuyo directorio autorizó “83 días después” de su designación la creación de la finiquitada entidad bancaria, explicaron los diputados en su acusación. Durante la administración de Peña, el Instituto de Previsión Social (IPS), una de las principales cajas pensionales del país, invirtió unos 355 millones de dólares en Ueno, que también administraba las cuentas de unos 32.000 jubilados. Por este caso, la Fiscalía también ha imputado a 27 personas, entre ellas Miguel Vásquez, uno de los fundadores de Ueno bank, quien este viernes fue trasladado junto a otros cinco directivos a cárceles para procesados.

articles.title: After the midterms, things are looking rocky for Elon Musk and data centers | TechCrunch
articles.summary: On Equity, we unpacked what the midterms mean for the tech industry.
articles.body_text: Democrats’ historic victory in this week’s midterm elections could also have a dramatic effect on the tech industry. In dozens of local ballot measures, voters rejected data centers . And even when they weren’t voting on the issue directly, they were electing politicians — like Texas’ new governor-elect Gina Hinojosa — who campaigned on the promise of restricting data centers. On the latest episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast , Kirsten Korosec, Sean O’Kane, and I discussed what the midterms mean for the tech industry. Sean kicked it off by noting that Elon Musk “seems to have basically nothing out of donating half a billion dollars” to Republicans, while his companies are now headquartered “in a state that has, remarkably, turned about as blue as it could possibly turn.” And Kirsten said that while data centers probably weren’t the main cause of the “blue wave,” they’ve become an “an increasingly grassroots issue, in part because of how hyperscalers and companies have gone about” getting their projects approved. And now, “we’re already seeing companies like OpenAI all of a sudden go, ‘Actually, we can change our policies.’” Keep reading for a preview of our conversation , edited for length and clarity. Sean O’Kane: First off, let’s talk about the fact that one of the biggest data center builders was also the largest donor to the Republican Party. Elon Musk seems to have gotten basically nothing out of donating half a billion dollars — maybe even more, by the time we see the final count — and in fact is now sitting there with all of his businesses in a state that has, remarkably, turned about as blue as it could possibly turn for the first time in a very long time, if ever. That, I think, is the biggest thing hanging above a lot of this discussion. But, there were also a bunch of ballot measures up around the country that would have paved the way for data centers to get built faster. Almost all of them got shot down, or voted against. [Actually, many of the ballot measures would have imposed restrictions or moratoriums on data centers, and almost all of those measures passed.] With [Democrats] in power, there is a consensus view, at least in the tech world, that this is going to mean we have a lot of roadblocks ahead for data centers, especially in places like Texas, where [you have] folks like the governor-elect [Gina] Hinojosa, who has spoken pretty openly about this being a campaign promise and something that she wants to focus on once she takes power, now that she’s beaten Greg Abbott. It’s the thing that I think the tech world is maybe a little too focused on. I’m curious what you guys think about that. Anthony Ha: I don’t necessarily think that they’re too focused on it, but I understand why it would feel a little bit disproportionate — the data center ballot measures, certainly there were a number of them, but it wasn’t something that was on the ballot everywhere. And in different races, the dynamic might have been a bit different, but there was this undercurrent and sense that it seems to be an issue that reaches across the country, that is bipartisan in a lot of ways, but that the Democrats seem to have been more effective at harnessing that energy. And of course, there’s all kinds of reasons why the Democrats did so well on Tuesday, but it does seem like anti-AI and especially anti-data center sentiment was a big part of it. That seems like a pretty potent political force. The next two years, [and] potentially beyond that, are going to be more difficult for tech companies in general, and hyperscalers, data center companies in particular. I also imagine that they have to be a little bit worried about: Is this going to continue to be an issue, not just with the people who got elected this year, but potentially in 2028 and beyond?

articles.title: Megaspeed exec was recruited to spy on Nvidia CEO, according to US intelligence memo | TechCrunch
articles.summary: A memo circulated earlier this year reportedly claimed that China’s Ministry of State Security recruited a female technology executive to spy on Nvidia's CEO.
articles.body_text: A memo circulated earlier this year claimed that technology executive Alice Huang was recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security to spy on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, according to multiple media reports. The New York Times, which had previously said Nvidia’s chief executive had been the target of Chinese intelligence, was the first to report on the memo , which was reportedly based on U.S. intelligence. The Financial Times subsequently reported that the memo also claimed Jensen Huang had a romantic relationship with Alice Huang, an executive at a Singapore-based company called Megaspeed. An Nvidia spokesperson told the NYT that Jensen Huang’s interactions with Alice Huang were “not unusual,” and that the company does not share classified information with its customers. A separate NYT report examined New Matrix, a Chinese company authorized by the U.S. Commerce Department to buy advanced Nvidia chips. But at the office address listed by New Matrix, reporters only found “a hollow gray shell,” raising concerns that it could be a front for a blacklisted private equity firm. articles.title: Parents want safer phones for kids. These companies are answering the call. | TechCrunch
articles.summary: As parents look for alternatives to unrestricted smartphones, a growing number of companies are building phones designed specifically for kids, from feature-limited mobile devices to minimalist home phones.
articles.body_text: As parents become increasingly concerned about the potential dangers of unrestricted smartphone access for children, a growing number of companies are developing devices specifically designed for kids. Today’s kid-friendly phones typically feature touchscreens, cameras, and communication capabilities similar to regular smartphones. However, the software on these devices is heavily modified to remove or restrict access to web browsers, social media, app stores, and other distractions. Parents can usually manage these devices through a companion app, allowing them to approve contacts, monitor locations, set screen time limits, select available apps, and, in some cases, receive alerts regarding cyberbullying, explicit content, or online predators. In addition to these modified devices, some companies offer a more minimalist approach, creating devices that focus solely on calling and texting. There are also home phones designed specifically for children, like Tin Can and the recently launched Pinwheel Home. Here’s a look at the major players shaping the kid-phone market. The Bark Phone is probably one of the most popular kid-specific smartphones on the market. Built on Samsung Galaxy hardware and powered by Bark’s monitoring software, it only allows calls and texts with approved contacts. Bark continuously scans texts, emails, photos, and supported apps for signs of cyberbullying, grooming, suicidal ideation, sexual content, and other potential concerns, then sends alerts to parents. A big standout feature is that parents can gradually unlock web browsing, apps, and other features as their child matures. The phone also includes GPS tracking and screen-time management. Current pricing for the standard model is $240 , plus a required wireless plan beginning at $29/month. Higher-tier plans add internet access and unlimited texting. Gabb is a well-known name in the kid-friendly phone category. Unlike Bark, however, Gabb focuses less on monitoring content and more on eliminating online risks altogether. Its phones don’t include social media, a browser, or an app store. Instead, children get calling, texting, and a carefully curated selection of preloaded apps, including a camera, calendar, and calculator. The company also touts its “worry-free” music streaming library with millions of songs.

articles.title: Binance CFO is leaving to 'pursue a new venture' after $6.3 billion hack | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The announcement comes barely more than a week after hackers stole $6.3 billion worth of cryptocurrency from Binance users.
articles.body_text: Binance’s chief financial officer Kaiser Ng is leaving the cryptocurrency exchange. According to Bloomberg , co-CEO Yi He said in a statement that Ng’s departure will allow him to “pursue a new venture after more than five years at Binance,” and that a transition plan has been “implemented over the last half year.” The announcement comes barely more than a week after hackers stole $6.3 billion worth of cryptocurrency from Binance users. The company froze withdrawals for several days; after accounts were unfrozen, users withdrew a net $3.6 billion in the first few hours. Binance and the FBI blamed a North Korean group called TraderTraitor for the hack. The company also said that it would cover all losses, promising, “Binance will bear the financial impact of the stolen funds. These losses will not be passed on to users.” Ng will be replaced as CFO by Justin Yek. articles.title: Amazon's new basic Kindle proves you don't need all the bells and whistles | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Amazon's redesigned basic Kindle costs more than before, but its lighter build and improved display make a compelling case for skipping the pricier models.
articles.body_text: In October, Amazon announced its refreshed Kindle lineup, its first significant design overhaul in years. The highlights included a new edge-to-edge design that eliminated traditional raised bezels, thinner and lighter Paperwhite and Colorsoft models with better displays, and page-turning accessories like a Bluetooth remote and a magnetic cover with page-turn buttons. However, given the impact of the global memory-chip shortage driven by the AI boom, the new Kindles also debuted with pricing that had increased by $40 to $50 across the lineup. That makes it more difficult for the average consumer to consider buying one of the more premium devices. For that reason, the Kindle I most wanted to get my hands on was the 6-inch entry-level device , which starts at $169.99 for the ad-free version. With the price hikes, this is the Kindle that will remain the most affordable to new e-reader buyers. The question I weighed was whether or not the basic Kindle is even worth buying at this price when there are arguably better Kindles on the market. The answer, after a couple of weeks of testing, is yes — if you can live without the bells and whistles and prefer a smaller, lighter device. On the 6-inch Kindle, there’s no warm light to reduce eye strain, no color display, no auto-adjusting brightness, no option to use the page-turn cover, and it’s not waterproof. Obviously, because of its size, the screen is smaller, as is the battery. Battery life is 6 weeks compared with the Paperwhite’s 12 weeks or Colorsoft’s 8 weeks. Still, even this basic Kindle has seen improvements of its own, mostly from a physical design perspective. The plastic 2026 Kindle is 11% lighter and 14% thinner than the 2024 model, weighing 140g versus 158g and measuring 6.85mm thick versus 8mm. While this seems like a small change, the 18-gram difference is noticeable and particularly welcome for a device you’re likely to carry in your purse or bag. Plus, it makes it easier to hold for hours on end when you’re really binging your way through a book. (The aluminum version, meanwhile, is slightly heavier at 162g, or 4 grams more than the 2024 Kindle, though it still benefits from the slimmer design.) And despite being the “starter” Kindle, the 6-inch basic device still received the new flush-front screen update. This makes it more comfortable to hold in your hand, especially for those long reading sessions. Amazon explained that you don’t have to worry about no longer having a bezel to rest your thumb upon, either, as the new Kindles have been updated to detect a dead zone in the capacitive touch that will readjust to account for the fact that your finger is there. In practice, that doesn’t mean you can just press your thumb down anywhere on the Kindle’s screen as you hold it — doing so would register this as an attempt to highlight or look up a word. Instead, it means you can rest your thumb or fingers on the outer edge of the Kindle’s screen (the colored border) without triggering an unintentional tap, even though some of your finger will be touching part of the Kindle’s capacitive screen. In terms of the software, the new basic Kindle is a bit snappier than its 2024 predecessor. This is most noticeable when opening books, which Amazon claims to be 30% faster. If you’re coming from the 2019 Kindle Basic, the 2026 version is an even bigger upgrade, as you gain USB-C, more storage (from 4GB to 8GB to now 16GB or 32GB), the new flush screen, and the screen resolution jumps from 167 ppi to 300 ppi. It’s faster, thinner, and lighter, too, and the battery lasts weeks longer.

articles.title: Sequoia shutting down its Scouts program marks the end of an era | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Sequoia pioneered the scouts model and many VC firms followed suit, but a consensus now seems to be forming that the model has reached limits in its current form.
articles.body_text: Sequoia this week announced a broad overhaul in a memo posted to X, a move that includes closing its London office and shutting down its scout program. Observers warn that it would be a mistake to read too much into the London closure, since the British capital has a thriving AI scene. On the other hand, the decision to end scouts says more about where venture investing is headed. That’s partly because 17 years ago, Sequoia pioneered the scouts model, in which select founders and operators write checks on the firm’s behalf. Amid increased competition for deal flow, many VC firms followed suit . But a consensus now seems to be emerging that the model has reached its limits in its current form. Not everyone was sold on the model in the first place. “They pioneered the scout program but [to be honest] it never made sense to me!” VC Sheel Mohnot wrote on X this week. “The scouts themselves don’t really care that much about the investments, you can still miss (like they did with Uber), not sure what it gets you. I suspect other firms will shutter theirs too,” he added. To be clear, Sequoia didn’t make a case against scouts in the memo. Instead, it framed its decision as part of a broader need for more focus. But its goal of “putting more energy behind fewer people and things” is likely to resonate with others who’ve questioned the ‘spray and pray’ approach to scouting. Rival firm Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), for instance, rolled out a global scout network aimed at spotting opportunities in the U.S. and also in smaller European hubs. But a16z partner Gabriel Vasquez told TechCrunch earlier this year that the firm had revamped its program to double down “on the best people.” Under this new approach, Vasquez explained, scouts get more resources but are also expected to be more active, such as by co-hosting dinners with the firm. “They get more budget, but we have reduced the number,” he said. This also seems to indicate that it is VC firms that have been driving an overhaul of the model. For founders, being a scout is attractive: it brings them closer to firms they may want checks from someday, or even a partner role with, and being seen as someone who can write a check can raise their standing among other founders. Some scouts will undoubtedly mourn the end of Sequoia’s program. Among them is Station F boss Roxanne Varza, who wrote on LinkedIn that she was “sad” to hear that the program was getting cut off, and “hope[d] that other funds [w]on’t follow suit.” Varza, a former Sequoia scout from 2020 to 2025, told TechCrunch that she had no information beyond what has been shared publicly, but observed that becoming a scout had often been a stepping stone for aspiring investment managers. “I cannot name all of the incredible scouts that have gone on to join or build funds, but there are quite a few. And the scout programs may have helped them get there — allowed them to build an investment track record, allowed them to build relationships with various funds directly, and more,” she wrote to TechCrunch. According to Varza, the program’s impact went beyond the individual level, instead helping the entire ecosystem become more mature. “I believe they have helped to foster the investment culture and early-stage investment landscape that we now see in Europe, for example,” Varza said. While others may agree with Varza about the role these programs have played, they may still have run their course for two reasons. First, seasoned operators may get more financial upside as angels. When it’s their own money, they get to keep the returns, too. Second, leading VC firms are now big and well-known enough that the best founders tend to come to them, so they worry less about missing deals, except at the very earliest stages or in niches and geographies where they have less reach.

articles.title: From the front row to the hot seat — what the midterms mean for Big Tech | TechCrunch
articles.summary: After spending two years getting cozy with the White House, Big Tech is suddenly trying to make friends with Democrats, and the open question is whether that image makeover can hold up against what states, local communities, and the markets are about to do.
articles.body_text: Right before the midterm elections, OpenAI hired Jessica Schumer , daughter of Democratic Sen. Chuck Schumer. The company also said it would start calling its data centers “ compute campuses .” For the past two years, many of Silicon Valley’s biggest names have built closer ties with President Donald Trump and his administration. Several attended White House events, some companies scaled back diversity, equity and inclusion programs, and some executives donated millions to super PACs supporting his campaign and allied candidates. Administration policies also benefited the industry, including tax breaks, the pausing of some federal investigations, and looser AI regulation. Meanwhile, Meta faced lawsuits and billion-dollar fines, and OpenAI faced suits alleging its technology harmed users. Now, with the midterms shifting the balance of power in Washington, those same companies are working to rebuild ties with Democrats, who have pledged to tighten oversight of AI. How far that gets them may depend less on image-polishing than on where the real fights are happening: in state capitols, in communities deciding whether to host data centers, and, as we’ve seen this past week, in the markets watching the AI boom. J.B. Branch, director of federal AI governance and technology policy at Public Citizen, a nonprofit advocacy group that describes itself as nonpartisan, told me that the tech industry “realizes they have an optics problem.” He characterized moves like the Schumer hire and the rebranding as “PR washing.” He expects more of it, too, pointing to OpenAI’s partnership with the American Federation of Teachers, announced last year, as well as Anthropic’s newly launched Claude Corps and Meta’s America’s Workforce Academy. “I would imagine more of that sort of investment in these corporate, private-public partnerships,” he said. These initiatives didn’t spring up overnight. Meta and other tech companies reportedly began looking for ways to strengthen their ties to Democrats as Democratic gains in the midterms looked more likely. Reached for comment about the midterm elections’ impact on Meta, a company spokesperson pointed TechCrunch to remarks that Meta President Dina Powell McCormick made this week at WSJ Tech. “You have to work with the government that the American people elect,” McCormick had said. “I have seen it across the board that you have to be bipartisan, and you want to be, because you want buy-in on the things that you’re trying to do.” Not everyone expects them to work. Alice Marwick, director of research at the tech policy nonprofit Data & Society, told me she expects Big Tech to try to pivot back toward the middle, “if not the left. But it’s a little too late,” she said. “Tech companies should be asking themselves how their products can make people’s lives better, because right now, it doesn’t seem like they are.” If Democrats follow through on pledges to tighten oversight of AI and Big Tech, the industry could face a tougher environment. Data center moratoriums are gaining traction, and a wave of AI regulation bills awaits drafting. At the same event, Powell McCormick said Meta wants to show that communities welcoming its investments will see “an enormous amount of benefit,” while those that don’t want them “will of course have the right to stop them.” Still, the next two years could bring political gridlock in Washington. Aryan Ranjan, founder of Baraza, a political campaign management software company, told me most action will likely happen at the state level, since states have already sued tech companies and passed regulations. “A coalition built on newer, working-class voters is likely to push Democrats to frame AI around electricity bills, data-center siting and jobs rather than abstract AI safety,” he said of what to expect at the federal level. Last December, the Trump administration signed an executive order creating the AI Litigation Task Force , a federal group meant to challenge state AI laws. The administration has argued that U.S. AI companies “must be free to innovate without cumbersome regulations.” Many states have nonetheless passed their own laws, including measures on chatbots and deepfakes. It also remains to be seen how President Trump will respond, including whether he’ll sign more AI executive orders or veto bills that could be seen as anti-AI. Clearly, voters want stronger guardrails around the technology. In a statement to TechCrunch, a White House official said: “American leadership in super intelligence is essential for our national security, economic prosperity, and the quality of life of the American people. President Trump is committed to ensuring America continues to lead the world in super intelligence while protecting American consumers. As the President has said, he’s willing to work with anyone to continue delivering victories for hardworking Americans.” Branch argued that Trump’s political fortunes are now tied to the AI industry. On Wednesday, the day after the midterms, a trillion-dollar market sell-off spooked investors, some are whom are reportedly now reconsidering Anthropic’s reported trillion-dollar IPO. “There’s a very strong likelihood that there will be an AI bubble pop, and it’ll happen on Trump’s hands,” Branch said, predicting a possible market collapse. “Does he want to sink or swim along with the AI industry?”

articles.title: Crusoe sells troubled Wyoming data center project to Google | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The deal highlights the challenges of developing massive AI data centers.
articles.body_text: Crusoe, an eight-year-old, Denver-based data center developer recently valued at $30.9 billion , confirmed Friday it has sold an unfinished data center project in southeastern Wyoming to Google. Google, which Crusoe had tried and failed to land as a customer for the project, is taking over the development after reportedly raising concerns about its cost and construction timeline under Crusoe’s management. Crusoe initially announced the project last year with Blackstone-backed infrastructure company Tallgrass, planning to eventually scale it to 10 gigawatts of power capacity. Google did not disclose how much it paid Crusoe for the unfinished project, but it announced plans to invest $17 billion to develop the data center campus. The deal highlights how difficult it can be for independent data center developers to deliver massive projects on time and within budget, given the challenges of securing equipment and power. Growing opposition from local communities can further complicate development. Despite taking over the Wyoming facility, Google hasn’t walked away from working with Crusoe entirely. Crusoe is developing another data center for Google near Amarillo, Texas. The deal to sell the site to Google was first reported by Bloomberg in June, but the Wyoming setback didn’t stop Crusoe from raising a $3.9 billion round in September. Crusoe makes money by leasing data center space to customers that bring their own GPUs, by renting out its own GPUs, and by selling compute power used to run AI models, known as inference. Crusoe’s largest projects serve some of the biggest names in AI. Its campus in Abilene, Texas, is being built in phases for Oracle and OpenAI, and the company is also constructing a separate 900-megawatt campus next door for Microsoft, with its first building expected to come online in mid-2027. Meta is also a customer, and Bloomberg reported that the trading firm Jane Street signed a $13 billion , five-year cloud deal with Crusoe. Crusoe was founded by Chase Lochmiller, now its CEO, and Cully Cavness, who started it as a cryptocurrency-mining business powered by natural gas that would otherwise have been burned off. In September, alongside its $3.9 billion funding round, the company added three board members , including JB Straubel, the Redwood Materials founder and Tesla board member who invested in Crusoe in 2021. Crusoe later became the first customer of Straubel’s energy-storage business. When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . This doesn’t affect our editorial independence. Marina Temkin is a venture capital and startups reporter at TechCrunch. Prior to joining TechCrunch, she wrote about VC for PitchBook and Venture Capital Journal. Earlier in her career, Marina was a financial analyst and earned a CFA charterholder designation.

articles.title: Ramp data shows AI spending stalling just as Anthropic nears its IPO | TechCrunch
articles.summary: AI usage keeps climbing, but spending has stalled. Price cuts and smarter cost controls among the biggest spenders could challenge investor assumptions about AI hypergrowth.
articles.body_text: Companies are using more AI than ever, but they’re not spending more on it. A new report from Ramp shows AI spending flatlined over late summer even as token volumes rose, a sign that price competition and savvier customers may be capping revenue for OpenAI and Anthropic. According to Ramp’s data, token spend only grew 1.5% across August and September. To compare, in July, it grew 42% from the previous month. As Anthropic gears up for its IPO , the data suggests investors might be wrong to assume AI companies will keep growing at breakneck speed. “Almost the entire spend on AI is from venture-backed, high-growth tech companies,” Ramp’s lead economist Ara Kharazian told TechCrunch. “That’s fine as long as AI spend continues to rise, but if it starts to slow down because of something in the market or some other factor, they will all start to slow down simultaneously, and that could lead to other cascading effects.” Kharazian said he’s already seeing evidence that the top 1% of firms — the most “ AI-pilled ” — have stuttered slightly in their spend in August and September, coming up just below the $10,000 per-employee they were hitting at their summer peaks. A slowdown among that cohort is “sufficient to slow down revenue entirely, despite the fact that we’re seeing rising volumes,” he said. Ramp data shows growth in spending among median and top 10%, but it’s not enough to make up the difference. Median firms spend $12-$15 per employee per month, and the top 10% spend $600-$1,000. “If you look at the use cases today, it’s not necessarily clear they will get up to that $10,000 per employee per month mark that the 1% is at,” Kharazian said. While there’s plenty of demand for AI coding agents in industries like software and finance, “it’s not necessarily true that a doctor’s office or a car dealership will need to spend that much on AI.” “The era of hypergrowth may be over, and now that we know there may not be as much juice to squeeze out of the top 1%,” he continued. October data did see a re-acceleration, with token spend up 8.9% from September 23 to October 23, but Kharazian said the headwinds on spend growth are strong. Kharazian (who has published a series of blogs called “ Cracks in the AI Thesis ”) said the slowdown isn’t due to a demand problem. Again, AI volumes are up. Instead he points to the competitive nature of the marketplace. “OpenAI and Anthropic price cuts have…just made it cheaper to use AI,” he said. In September, OpenAI cut API prices in half for GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna. Answering the price war, Anthropic has also made significant reductions to pricing for Fable 5.1 and Opus 5.5 — a decision that the company said in a recent filing slashed revenue growth by about $600 million. Both companies have also been offering enterprise discounts that are intended to lock-in spend, but in reality are hitting their revenue targets. Kharazian said this dynamic means it has very much become a buyer’s market.

articles.title: Tesla will stop making the Cybertruck in 2027 | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The decision to wind down the EV comes after just a few short years of underwhelming sales. Elon Musk said the company will use the factory space to make more Cybercabs.
articles.body_text: Tesla will stop making the Cybertruck next year, according to CEO Elon Musk, who said on X that the company will use the factory space to build more two-seater Cybercab robotaxis. The decision to wind down the futuristic, steel-clad EV comes after just a few short years of underwhelming sales. When Musk handed over the first few Cybertrucks in late 2023, he predicted Tesla would sell around 250,000 per year. It was supposed to be such a cornerstone of Tesla’s future that, before construction began, the company talked about its Texas factory as the “Cybertruck factory.” But Tesla has instead sold just tens of thousands — total — over the last three years. Tesla is killing off the Cybertruck at a moment when it is trying to become an AI- and robotics-focused company. A big part of that is its robotaxi ambitions. The company has spent the last two months putting Cybercabs on the streets in its hometown of Austin, Texas. With no major incidents to date, the company has said it plans to expand the Cybercabs operations to other cities, starting with Dallas later this month. (Tesla also operates robotaxi versions of its Model Y SUVs in Austin, Houston, and Dallas, as well as three cities in Florida.) This is the third product Tesla has discontinued in order to fuel those greater ambitions. Earlier this year, the company decided to end production of the Model S sedan and Model X SUV and instead use the factory space dedicated to those vehicles to make Optimus humanoid robots. First announced in 2019, the Cybertruck was a product that Musk had long obsessed over. “Probably my personal favorite for the next product is the pickup truck, and we are going to just do an amazing pickup truck,” he said on one of Tesla’s earnings calls that year. Musk promised the Cybertruck would be radical, inspired by the designs of cyberpunk sci-fi stories like “Blade Runner.” While that certainly bore out in the design, the company overpromised on the basics of the Cybertruck from the jump. During the now-infamous reveal event in 2019, when head designer Franz von Holzhausen cracked the Cybertruck’s windows with steel balls, Tesla said the EV was supposed to start at under $40,000 and have up to 500 miles of range. It achieved neither of those figures. Instead, the truck was delayed for two years, in part because of the COVID-19 pandemic. When it finally did hit the market in late 2023, Tesla handed over the first few Cybertrucks to customers in a short, somewhat odd for Tesla event (by the company’s own standards, at least), which saw a poorly-lit Musk standing in a truck bed promising the truck was “the finest in apocalyptic equipment” fit for “late civilization vibes.” The base price had inflated to around $60,000, and the top-end range had shrunk by over 100 miles. The truck has struggled on the market ever since. The polarizing design never seemed to sit well with buyers, especially at a higher-than-expected price. Then, during its first full year of sales in 2024, Musk became a major financial backer of Donald Trump, which turned the instantly recognizable Cybertruck into a target for protesters. That continued into 2025 as Musk led the so-called Department of Government Efficiency, which fired thousands of federal workers. articles.title: 3D DRAM created by IBM and Micron, 128GBps memory on the way
articles.summary: Smaller and faster RAM with up to 128GB transfer speed scould be on the way thanks to research from IBM and MIcron, using stacked chips and TSVs.
articles.body_text: Smaller and faster RAM with up to 128GBps transfer speeds could be on the way thanks to research from IBM and MIcron. The companies have developed three-dimensional memory, stacking individual DRAM chips vertically that would normally have to be placed side-by-side, though the efficiencies gained aren’t solely down to space. Communication between the stacked chips and the host device is achieved through a new creation known as through-silicon vias, or TSVs, which run vertically through the pile of chips and act as conduits to the host device. Thanks to the TSVs, in testing the memory has reached data speeds of 128GBps, ten times faster than current memory. On top of this, IBM claims the chips are 70 percent more power efficient than today’s DRAM. The new research is expected to form a key part of Samsung and Micron’s Hybrid Memory Cube technology, first announced back in October. IBM and Micron hope to have commercial availability in two years, with servers likely to use it first. Looking beyond that, IBM fellow Subu Iyer said that the new process “will have applications beyond memory, enabling other industry segments as well.” What exactly those new segments are remains to be seen, but we certainly wouldn’t complain if our computers got the kind of speed bump described here.
